text: The [definition](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Convolution.lean#L159) first applies s and t to the two tensor legs, then multiplies in S. On x⊗y this gives exactly s(x)t(y), in that order. This agrees with the tensor-map/multiplication formula underlying [Mathlib convolution](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Coalgebra/Convolution.lean#L56). No coalgebra structure is needed for this exterior product, and S may be noncommutative. The published zero and addition formulas also pass.
A zero first map gives the zero exterior product.
Distributivity in the second map preserves the specified product order.

On a pure tensor x⊗y, the left side is g(xy), while the [exterior-product formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Convolution.lean#L166) makes the right side g(x)g(y). Algebra-homomorphism multiplicativity identifies them, exactly as [Mathlib’s postcomposition calculation](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Coalgebra/Convolution.lean#L176) uses the multiplication compatibility. Tensor extensionality gives the stated linear-map equality. Neither a coalgebra nor a commutative target is required; this is multiplicativity transported through the WithConv type tag.
Evaluation identifies the right-hand side as the ordered product of the two images.

For Δ(h)=∑h₁⊗h₂, the claimed equality reads φ(Δ(h))=∑φ(h₁⊗1)φ(1⊗h₂). Multiplicativity of φ proves it, matching [Mathlib’s convolution of algebra maps](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Bialgebra/Convolution.lean#L50). Only its target A must be commutative for those points to form a convolution monoid; H may be noncommutative. The [published tensor-square point specialization](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Convolution.lean#L133) passes when H is commutative.
Taking the identity on a commutative tensor square gives the native inclusion-product formula.

This equivalence sends φ:C→B′ to the coordinate maps c↦coordᵢ(φ(c)); its inverse reconstructs the value by the finite basis expansion. [Mathlib’s basis equivalence](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Basis/Defs.lean#L240) supplies both inverse identities, matching the [source construction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Convolution.lean#L269). Finite indexing is essential because the target allows arbitrary coordinate families. B′ only needs its module structure here: WithConv is a type tag, and no convolution multiplication or coalgebra on C is asserted.
The actual forward coordinate formula fixes the index and coefficient direction.
The actual inverse reassembles the family using the finite basis equivalence.

In the convolution monoid of algebra maps H→H⊗H, the two inclusion points multiply to Δ: on tensor terms, (h₁⊗1)(1⊗h₂)=h₁⊗h₂. This is [Mathlib’s algebra-map convolution](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Bialgebra/Convolution.lean#L50), and the [published postcomposition theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Convolution.lean#L105) gives the displayed equality with φ=id. Commutativity of H ensures the tensor-square target is commutative; cocommutativity of Δ and an antipode are unnecessary.
The general published postcomposition identity specializes to this exact comultiplication point.

[Convolution](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Coalgebra/Convolution.lean#L56) sends the ordered inclusion pair to μ((includeLeft⊗includeRight)(Δ(c))). The middle linear map is the identity because (x⊗1)(1⊗y)=x⊗y, exactly the [source tensor calculation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Convolution.lean#L71). Hence the result is Δ itself. CoalgebraStruct correctly suffices: only the comultiplication map is used, with no coassociativity or antipode law. The [published bialgebra postcomposition consequence](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Convolution.lean#L105) passes.
The algebra-point theorem consumes this weaker linear identity without adding commutativity to its source.

The ith component is precisely coordᵢ∘φ, with the B-linear coordinate map restricted to R using the scalar tower. This is the [actual forward function](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Convolution.lean#L274), and [Mathlib’s coordinate definition](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Basis/Defs.lean#L663) fixes which coefficient is extracted. The [published inverse formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Convolution.lean#L304) reconstructs the same family. The statement concerns underlying linear maps; no multiplicativity of coordinates or coalgebra structure on C is assumed.
The inverse rebuilds the family with the same coordinate order and scalar restriction.

Expanding both [convolutions](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Coalgebra/Convolution.lean#L56) on the tensor-product comultiplication gives s(c₁)t(d₁)u(c₂)v(d₂). Commutativity of S permits the middle factors to exchange, yielding (s*u)(c)(t*v)(d), exactly the displayed interleaving identity. [Mathlib’s tensor-convolution compatibility](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Coalgebra/Convolution.lean#L87) supplies the formal calculation. The two source modules can differ and need only comultiplication data. The published pure-tensor and zero formulas pass; no multiplication on either source is assumed.
Pure-tensor evaluation fixes which map acts on each of the two distinct source legs.
The zero right leg gives the expected degenerate exterior product.

[Postcomposition](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Coalgebra/Convolution.lean#L243) embeds f’s coefficients through B→B′. Expanding its convolution with φ, B-linearity of coordᵢ gives coordᵢ(∑f(c₁)φ(c₂))=∑f(c₁)coordᵢ(φ(c₂)), exactly the right side. The [source proof](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Convolution.lean#L319) checks pure tensors and addition. The published coordinate and reconstruction formulas pass. This asserts linearity for the left convolution action, not that arbitrary basis coordinates preserve products in B′.
The coordinate extracted on each side is the same restricted scalar coordinate.
Reconstruction verifies the underlying coefficient-module identification.

The value is μ_S∘(s⊗t), so a pure tensor x⊗y maps to s(x)t(y), exactly the advertised exterior product. This is the tensor-map and multiplication part of [Mathlib’s convolution formula](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Coalgebra/Convolution.lean#L56), before precomposition with any comultiplication. Its [published evaluation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Convolution.lean#L166), zero and additivity equations pass. The codomain may be noncommutative because the order is fixed, and no coalgebra structure is incorrectly required merely to define this map.
The defining operation evaluates pure tensors legwise in the stated order.
A zero first factor yields zero.
The product is additive in the second map.

The [carrier](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/UniversalCover/RealProjective/Basic.lean#L58) is the unit sphere modulo antipodes with its quotient topology, exactly the model in [Hatcher, Examples 0.4 and 2.42](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=153). Lean gives actual singular homology with constant left-regular coefficients, not a separately defined cellular substitute. The [published comparison](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Cellular/RealProjective/Homology.lean#L177) and [boundary calculation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Cellular/RealProjective/Basic.lean#L350) give zero outgoing differential and incoming image `R ∙ 2` for odd `k < N`. This remains correct for noncommutative rings: 2 is central, and the proof removes the orientation unit explicitly.

The [roadmap’s cellular calculation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/4f7a4021c5eefb6a254dcd4db450663a5f1aa71d/TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicTopology/README.md#L789) passes in the source; [characteristic-two vanishing](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Cellular/RealProjective/Homology.lean#L80) and the published integral specialization also pass. Its additional Projectivization homeomorphism and smooth-atlas work are separate integration targets, not assertions of this homology equivalence. My earlier hold imposed that extra requirement incorrectly. No new diagnostic proof is substituted for a published Check.
Native cellular boundary is zero out of odd positive degree; the theorem indexes the target cell by even i.
Native integral boundary out of positive even degree is ±2, exactly the roadmap allowance for generator signs.
Published characteristic-two family computes every native cellular differential as zero.
Companion integral calculation verifies zero positive even-degree singular homology, including above the top dimension.

The actual projection p:A→H(A) is a quasi-isomorphism, so p∘f is one between minimal A∞ algebras. Minimality makes its linear part bijective, and the [constructed two-sided A∞ inverse](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/AInfinity/Algebra/Hom/Iso.lean#L91) gives exactly IsIso, matching [Keller §3.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9910179#page=7)’s nonunique minimal-model isomorphism. The published [p∘i=id](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/AInfinity/Algebra/Transfer/Cohomology.lean#L608) and [cohomology identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/AInfinity/Algebra/Transfer/Cohomology.lean#L618) checks pass. The [quiver Ext example](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/a8132fb235144b25aba003881cc74e35d7d15f36/TauCetiRoadmap/DGAInfinity/README.md#L744) tests the separate transfer computation; it is not a uniqueness check. The chosen projection is noncanonical, and no finite-dimensionality, formality, or derived-module equivalence is asserted.
The actual transferred projection is a quasi-isomorphism, so its composite with the given f is a quasi-isomorphism.
The actual projection composed with the actual inclusion equals the identity A∞ morphism; this fixes composition direction and normalization.
The projection induces the identity under the native minimal-cohomology identification.
Between minimal algebras a quasi-isomorphism is a genuine A∞ isomorphism, not only a cohomology isomorphism.
The constructed inverse satisfies the left inverse equation as an A∞ morphism.
The constructed inverse also satisfies the right inverse equation as an A∞ morphism.
